name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.202.0 — Gates, per workspace: /spec:enforce now discovers and wires enforcers once per workspace, not once per repo — a new workspace-scan.js walks the tree for package manifests, the enforce cell grammar gains workspace (and, for naming, a layer of code/schema/routes/wire), and the grounding contract's Rule enforcement section states the (workspace x stack x category) entry shape and id grammar; a monorepo with a Python API and a TypeScript frontend now gets its own checker set per workspace, with naming enforced per layer from the host naming table, and every checker wired to run from its own workspace root inside the one gate string. 7.201.0 — The design contract is code: a host with a UI stack now declares design: {kit, tokens, rules} in its grounding config instead of a single app pointer, and design-contract-check.js is the mechanical presence oracle — it walks the kit directory for intent-named composites, parses the rules file's intent-to-pattern and per-layer naming tables, and reports every gap by kind and remedy. /spec:init locates the three paths and seeds the rules file from a template when absent, running the check as an advisory report rather than a gate; /spec:doctor check 8 runs the same script; /spec:enforce gains the kit-discipline category (folding color/typography/density out of the old forbidden-symbol/structural-pattern split) so a host's kit-backed design rules get a real discovered enforcer alongside everything else. No doctrine prose enforces any of this — the check script and the taxonomy are the only oracles. 7.200.0 — The approval file is not a gate: the per-brief design workbench command and the plan-to-build design stage are deleted along with their frontmatter contract fields, and every plan/run/build/review/status reader of design/approval.json; the three lanes a change can travel (direct, behaviour, structural) are now written once in core.md's Pipeline Entry doctrine. /spec:mocks and genesis are unaffected — they keep writing and reading design/approval.json.
